title: Repackaging Dedicated GPU Plans for Demand Smoothing and SLA Differentiation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a simplified set of dedicated GPU SKUs that smooth demand by incentivizing off-peak reservations, add explicit SLA tiers, and pilot elastic burst credits. This ticket outlines the experiment matrix, contract language updates, and security questionnaire (SQ) implications for enterprise customers.
background: Current Dedicated offering has high variance in committed utilization and multiple ad-hoc burst policies. Sales and Finance report friction in multi-quarter contracts and customers ask for clearer SLA tiers with explicit remedies. Engineering is evaluating autoscaling and smart burst enforcement but needs predictable commitment profiles to size pools.
proposed_solution: 1) Create three commitment bands (Baseline, Flex, Priority) with clear throughput guarantees and latency SLOs. 2) Introduce off-peak discounts and transferable burst credits to smooth demand. 3) Define explicit canary/rollback rules for model rollouts in Priority tier. 4) Publish pricing matrix and sample contract addendum for legal review.
experiment_design: We will run a 12-week pilot with 10 existing mid-market customers across the three bands. Assign five customers to off-peak discount variant (price/time-shift incentives) and five to burst-credit pilot. Track utilization smoothing and churn. Variants: A) Baseline (status quo), B) Time-shift discount, C) Burst-credit with soft caps and automated throttles.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least 15% reduction in 95th-percentile per-customer peak utilization compared to baseline for pilot cohort.
- No more than 2 customer escalations related to availability during pilot.
- Legal approves standard contract addendum and SQ responses for new packaging.
- Engineering confirms autoscale policy can enforce burst credit limits without SLA violations.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: Off-peak discounts reduce revenue if demand shifts are ephemeral.
- Trade-off: Tighter burst caps improve predictability but may increase customer churn for latency-sensitive workloads.
- Risk: New contract language may lengthen legal review cycles for enterprise deals.
- Operational cost: implementing burst-credit accounting and enforcement requires runtime changes and billing pipeline updates.
contract_and_sq_notes: Work with Legal to add an addendum template: include committed GPU units, burst credit bucket mechanics, overage pricing, and SLA remedies per tier. Update standard SQ answers to reflect: encryption at rest for customer keys, audit log retention, region isolation options for Priority tier, and KMS/HSM support. Flag: Priority tier requires SOC2-plus attestation paragraph in SQ.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: finalize pricing matrix and legal addendum (2 weeks). Phase 1: pilot with 10 customers (12 weeks). Phase 2: evaluate results and iterate pricing. Phase 3: GA launch with self-serve options and enterprise onboarding flows. Include a controlled enablement in Console: toggle for off-peak scheduling and burst credit view.
